metaDescription: New Milford, PA sits in Susquehanna County's dry-gas Marcellus core near the New York border. We buy mineral rights directly, no broker, no waiting.
heroLead: New Milford sits close enough to the New York state line in Susquehanna County that the contrast between the two states' approach to shale gas is impossible to miss here.
intro: Susquehanna County has some of the strongest dry-gas Marcellus rock anywhere in Pennsylvania, and operators developed acreage around New Milford aggressively during the play's most active years. Just a short distance north, across the border, that same formation has stayed largely untouched due to New York's restrictions on high-volume fracturing.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around New Milford directly. We'll confirm your parcel's exact location and research its full title history before making an offer.

sections.heading: A Border County With Strong Production History
paragraphs: New Milford and the surrounding townships have seen sustained, strong Marcellus production for well over a decade, and Susquehanna County wells have generally ranked among the state's most productive. If your family's interest has been part of an active unit that long, there's real production history to evaluate.
As dry-gas territory, statements here don't carry liquids-processing deductions, though standard gathering and compression costs still apply.

sections.heading: Confirming Border-Area Title
paragraphs: We research your chain of title through the Susquehanna County Recorder of Deeds in Montrose, confirming your parcel sits on the Pennsylvania side of the line where that's relevant, since Pennsylvania's royalty protections apply only to Pennsylvania leases.
Older surveys near the border sometimes use reference points that predate modern parcel mapping, and we take the time to reconcile that during title research.

sections.heading: What We'll Walk You Through
paragraphs: Before discussing an offer, we'll review your division order, lease terms, and royalty history with you so the full picture is clear.

faqs.question: Why has drilling stopped at the New York border near New Milford?
faqs.answer: New York restricts high-volume hydraulic fracturing statewide, so Marcellus development has largely stopped at the state line even though the same formation continues north.

faqs.question: Is New Milford still an active area for Marcellus production?
faqs.answer: Susquehanna County has been one of the strongest-producing counties in the play, and we check current activity specific to your unit as part of our review.

faqs.question: My deed uses old survey reference points near the border. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It can slow research slightly, but it's common in this part of the county and not a barrier to confirming clean title.

faqs.question: Does a strong statewide production ranking mean my specific well is strong too?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. We evaluate your specific well and unit's actual trailing royalty history rather than assuming county-level performance applies to every parcel.

faqs.question: What should I gather before reaching out?
faqs.answer: Your deed, your lease if you have it, and recent division order or royalty statements are the most useful documents to start with.
